section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the two opposite aspects of Shabbat: that it receives from the six weekdays as Malchus, yet also blesses them after its ascent.
section.t: And it can be said that this is also the explanation of what is brought
(at the beginning of the maamar)
two extremes regarding the matter of Shabbat,
that Shabbat is called a queen, which is the Sefirah of Malchus that is lower than all the Sefiros and receives from them,
as per the statement
"The moon has nothing of its own,"
[and as per the statement of our sages, of blessed memory,
(regarding Shabbat)
"Only one who toiled on Erev Shabbat will eat on Shabbat"],
and on the other hand, "all the days are blessed from Shabbat,"
meaning that not only is Shabbat holy from all the days,
but moreover,
it influences them.
However, the explanation is,
that the seven days of the week are the seven days of construction,
for the six weekdays are in Zeir Anpin, as it is written,
"Six days did Hashem make the heavens and the earth," and it is brought in the Zohar,
"Each day does its work,"
and Shabbat is Malchus
(as above).
Therefore,
from this aspect, that Malchus descended below,
and especially from the aspect of its descent into Biyah, "her legs descend" etc.,
Shabbat
(Malchus)
receives from the six weekdays
(Zeir Anpin),
which is the matter of the work of refinement
(the refinement of the Nefesh HaBahamis and all physical things)
of the six weekdays.
However, after
(and through)
this work, there is accomplished
(on Shabbat)
the ascent of Malchus from Biyah until its ascent to its source and origin,
and then it ascends above Zeir Anpin until it also influences all six weekdays
(Zeir Anpin),
for "from it all the days are blessed."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the verse "Come my beloved to greet the bride," as the drawing down of Zeir Anpin into Malchus, which also elevates the receiver to become a crown for the giver.
section.t: And this is "Come my beloved to greet the bride; let us welcome the face of Shabbat,"
which is the request of the Neshama of Yisrael that there be a drawing down of Zeir Anpin into Malchus.
For the beginning of the drawing down is "Come my beloved to greet the bride,"
a mere going,
and through this "let us welcome the face of Shabbat,"
which is the inner drawing down,
"the face of Shabbat,"
that reveals the aspect of the innerness of Malchus, even as it is rooted in Atik.
And therefore "let us welcome" is in the plural,
for Zeir Anpin also receives from
(the root of)
Malchus,
"a woman of valor is the crown of her husband."
And just as it is above in Zeir Anpin and Malchus,
so too is it with every influencer and receiver,
that through the receiver, addition is brought to the influencer,
and "from my students more than from all of them."
And especially with a groom and bride below,
that specifically through the inner drawing down,
behold "a woman of valor is the crown of her husband,"
and "everything was from the dust."
For through this, the power of Ein Sof is drawn down, "a generation of the upright shall be blessed," with sons and grandsons engaged in Torah and mitzvos.
